evidence_policy.note: This matrix indexes normative and architectural claims. It is not packet-capture evidence and does not claim a public or production test.

scoring.meaning: Qualitative design pressure, not a benchmark or compliance result.

entries.name: NAT
security_and_limits: NAT is not inherently a firewall
UDP timeout and filtering behavior vary
CGN requires operational logging and creates attribution/privacy costs

entries.name: Stateful firewall
security_and_limits: an open port result is local to an interface, address family, policy and time
logs are local observations, not proof of endpoint delivery
state capacity and timeout are implementation/configuration limits

entries.name: Application proxy
changes: one connection becomes two trust relationships
security_and_limits: TLS termination changes the trust boundary
cache correctness depends on freshness, Vary, authorization and Cache-Control
proxy behavior is not a generic repair for non-proxy-aware protocols

entries.name: Load balancing
security_and_limits: health checks only establish a narrow point-in-time condition
equal connection counts do not imply equal work
Anycast convergence and path changes can move clients
PROXY metadata requires a trusted ingress

entries.name: Content delivery network
security_and_limits: wrong cache keys can leak cross-user data
CDN does not guarantee low latency, strong consistency or availability
purge is generally provider control-plane behavior, not an HTTP guarantee
edge encryption does not define one universal trust model

museum.name: Middlebox Museum
museum.thesis: Middleboxes improve deployability and policy control while introducing state, hidden topology, extra trust anchors and protocol compatibility costs.

exhibits.distortion: addresses and ports are not stably visible
exhibits.end_to_end_question: who can initiate inbound state and when does mapping expire?

exhibits.distortion: reachability depends on policy and state
exhibits.end_to_end_question: are failure signals and PMTUD messages preserved?

exhibits.distortion: one connection becomes separate trust relationships
exhibits.end_to_end_question: who terminates TLS and sees application semantics?

exhibits.distortion: service identity is separated from backend identity
exhibits.end_to_end_question: how do affinity, failure convergence and capacity interact?

exhibits.distortion: responses may come from cache rather than origin
exhibits.end_to_end_question: what are freshness, invalidation and privacy boundaries?
